title: Compatibility proxy for embeddings & rerank: unify pagination mapping, error canonicalization, and streaming parity
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: add a short-lived compatibility proxy that sits in front of the new embeddings/rerank endpoints to provide parity with legacy clients. The proxy must normalize pagination semantics (cursor vs link-header), canonicalize historical HTTP error payloads and status codes clients expect, and offer an opt-in streaming facade that mirrors legacy chunking for streaming clients. This avoids forcing customers to upgrade many SDKs at once while we complete a long-term API convergence plan.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts legacy cursor param and Link header pagination and returns stable cursors that remain valid for 30 days
Error mappings reproduce legacy error JSON shape and legacy status codes for documented error classes (rate_limit, auth_error, quota_exceeded, server_failure)
Streaming facade emits legacy chunk envelopes for existing clients without changing new endpoint internals
All request/response transformations are logged and traceable in Console with a toggle to disable proxy per-customer
Automated test suite covers pagination edge cases (empty pages, tombstone cursors, final page, jumping cursors) and runs in CI with mocked services
implementation_plan: 1) Design transform matrix for cursor<->link semantics (Luca + Priya). 2) Implement proxy middleware in gateway service (ENG-gateway) with a feature flag per-customer. 3) Add canonical error mapper module and integrate with runtime error classifier. 4) Implement streaming adapter that converts new streaming event packets to legacy chunk envelopes. 5) Add telemetry (transform counts, mapped errors) and dashboard. 6) Run compatibility job against 50k historical requests to detect mismatches. 7) Gradual rollout: internal -> opt-in beta customers -> platform-wide.
decisions: Use opaque stable cursor tokens (base64 HMAC) rather than reusing internal shard offsets to avoid leaking topology

Map legacy client '429' rate limit responses to the same JSON payload shape including 'retry_after_seconds' field; new internal quota errors will still emit 429 but with internal detail in an 'x-internal' header when flag enabled
Prefer Link header production for new clients; proxy will synthesize Link header for legacy cursor-based requests so both styles are available
Streaming adapter will rely on a small sidecar process to minimize latency impact on the primary runtime rather than adding per-request branching in the hot path
risks: Statefulness of stable cursors requires key rotation strategy - lost keys could invalidate many cursors
Extra latency introduced by proxy path (target <= 12ms median added); risk for latency-sensitive customers on Dedicated
Edge cases where legacy clients expect non-idempotent cursor reuse semantics (we'll emulate but must document behavior)
Mapping errors incorrectly might hide upstream failures (we must keep internal headers for SRE debugging)
Streaming sidecar scaling needs capacity on high-concurrency bursts
testing_plan: Unit tests for serializer/mapping, integration tests against staging embed/rerank runtime, load test using replay of anonymized 50k historical requests, fuzz tests for malformed cursor tokens, and a canary run to 3 beta workspaces with traffic split 5%/20%/50% during rollout phases.
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): deploy to staging + 2 internal teams for 1 week. Phase B (beta): enable proxy for 5 opt-in customers with traffic mirroring for 72h, then 5% production traffic for 48h. Phase C (wider opt-in): open toggle in Console per workspace. Phase D (opt-out deprecation): after 90 days, announce sunsetting of legacy endpoints with migration guide and final cutover plan.
